---
760	By the FGA route (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.*`), `Pic⁰_{C/k}` is representable
761	(`Scheme.PicScheme.representable`) and is an abelian variety of dimension `genus C`:
762	its tangent space at the identity is `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` (`Scheme.Pic0.tangentSpaceIso`),
763	giving smoothness of relative dimension `genus C` (`Scheme.Pic0.smooth`), properness
764	(`Scheme.Pic0.proper`), and geometric irreducibility
765	(`Scheme.Pic0.geometricallyIrreducible`); the Albanese universal property is the
766	Abel–Jacobi factorisation of `AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.AlbaneseUP`.
767	
768	The genus-`0` case is **not** special and needs no separate construction: when
769	`genus C = 0` the tangent space is `0`-dimensional, so `Pic⁰_{C/k} = Spec k`
770	automatically, and the universal property degenerates to the (then trivial) statement
771	that every pointed morphism `C ⟶ A` into an abelian variety is constant. The former
772	`genusZeroWitness` / `positiveGenusWitness` genus split — together with its bespoke
773	rigidity / cotangent-vanishing / Frobenius / `ℙ¹`-identification machinery — has been
774	removed in favour of this single uniform witness.
775	
776	**No hypothesis on `C(k)`.** The binders are exactly the three challenge hypotheses, which
777	is the owner decision of 2026-07-28 (protection I-0491) and the full strength the challenge
778	asks for. This is *not* a specialisation of
779	`picardJacobianWitnessOfHasRationalPoint`: it is wired to the **étale** Picard development,
780	with underlying scheme `Scheme.Pic0SchemeEt C` — the identity component of the scheme
781	representing the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor (`Picard/Pic0Et.lean`,
782	`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`). Sheafifying is what removes the rational point:
783	the unsheafified functor is not a sheaf, so representability of it over an arbitrary field
784	would be a *false* statement rather than an unproved one.
785	
786	Four of the six witness fields come from theorems that are proved **unconditionally** and
787	measure axiom-clean (`Pic0Et.grpObj`, `Pic0Et.geometricallyIrreducible`, and through them
788	`Pic0Et.locallyOfFiniteType` / `Pic0Et.isSeparated`). This definition carries no `sorry` of
789	its own, but that is a statement about this file, not a completeness claim: it depends on
790	the five obligations enumerated in the file header —
791	`Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability`, `Scheme.Pic0Et.geometricallyReduced`,
792	`Scheme.Pic0Et.universallyClosed`, `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0Et` and
793	`isAlbanese_pic0Et` — every one of which is a **true statement awaiting a proof**.
794	
795	**These five are not five independent distances, and counting them as such
796	overstates the remaining work by one while understating what leaf B buys**
797	(measured by `ajc-p3`, independently by `ajc-p2`, relayed here by `review-ajc`
798	because both lanes declined to edit a third lane's file mid-round; `I-1044`).
799	`SmoothOfRelativeDimension.geometricallyReduced` turns obligation 4
800	(`smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0Et`) directly into obligation 2
801	(`Pic0Et.geometricallyReduced`), and composed with
802	`Pic0Et.smooth_of_geometricallyReduced` it also gives `Pic0Et.smooth`. So the
803	arrow runs 4 ⟹ 2: no work on 2 is wasted, but closing leaf B closes two of the
804	five at once. Still genuinely independent: `Pic0Et.universallyClosed`, whose
805	residue is `IsReduced`-free and which nothing in the smoothness cone touches. The
806	`GeometricallyIntegral` hypothesis of the Picard development is *not* among them: it is
807	synthesised from the challenge hypotheses through `Smooth.geometricallyIntegral` (see
808	`geometricallyIntegral_of_curve`). -/
809	noncomputable def picardJacobianWitness (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
810	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
811	    JacobianWitness C where
812	  J := Scheme.Pic0SchemeEt C
813	  grpObj := (Scheme.Pic0Et.grpObj C).some
814	  proper := Scheme.Pic0Et.proper C
815	  smooth := Scheme.Pic0Et.smooth C
816	  geomIrred := Scheme.Pic0Et.geometricallyIrreducible C
817	  smoothGenus := smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0Et C
818	  isAlbaneseFor := fun P => isAlbanese_pic0Et C _ _ _ _ P
819	
820	/-- **The witness over an algebraically closed field: a genuine `k̄` theorem.**
821	
822	The same assembly as `picardJacobianWitnessOfHasRationalPoint`, with the rational point
823	supplied by the theorem `hasRationalPoint_of_curve_of_isAlgClosed` rather than assumed. Over
824	`k̄` a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve really does have a rational point — the
825	curve is a nonempty Jacobson space and its closed points are rational — so this definition
826	records what the `picSharp` route actually reaches, with nothing false anywhere in it.
827	
828	**It is not the headline** (owner decision of 2026-07-28, protection I-0491 clause 4). It is
829	a theorem about algebraically closed base fields, and the challenge asks for an arbitrary
830	one; that statement is `picardJacobianWitness`, which is built on the étale-sheafified
831	functor and does not pass through this definition or through
832	`picardJacobianWitnessOfHasRationalPoint`.
833	
834	Its obligations are those of the `picSharp` route with the rational point discharged:
835	`Scheme.picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`'s content (i.e. `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability`),
836	`Pic0.smooth`, `Pic0.proper`, and the two `picSharp`-shaped leaves
837	`smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0` / `isAlbanese_pic0`. Discharging the rational point
838	does not remove the representability gate — it makes it *fire* instead of being assumed,
839	since `Scheme.Pic0Scheme` carries `[Scheme.HasPicScheme C]` — so the count does not shrink
840	here either. What it buys is that every obligation is of the ordinary kind.
841	
842	Both are kept: this one records what the `picSharp` route reaches over `k̄`, and the
843	headline states what the project claims over an arbitrary field. -/
844	noncomputable def picardJacobianWitnessOfIsAlgClosed [IsAlgClosed k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
845	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
846	    JacobianWitness C :=
847	  haveI := hasRationalPoint_of_curve_of_isAlgClosed C
848	  picardJacobianWitnessOfHasRationalPoint C
849	
850	/-- Existence of an Albanese witness for every smooth proper geometrically irreducible
851	curve, uniformly in the genus via the Picard identity component `Pic⁰_{C/k}`
852	(`picardJacobianWitness`). This packages the five protected obligations (`Jacobian`,
853	`instGrpObj`, `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus`, `instIsProper`,
854	`instGeometricallyIrreducible`) into a single existence statement, and records that the
855	Albanese property of the underlying scheme `J` is uniform over every choice of
856	`k`-rational marked point `P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C` (via the `isAlbaneseFor` field of
857	`JacobianWitness`). -/
858	theorem nonempty_jacobianWitness (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
859	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
860	    Nonempty (JacobianWitness C) :=
861	  ⟨picardJacobianWitness C⟩
862	
863	/-- A choice of Albanese witness for `C`, extracted via `Classical.choice`.
864	Used to define `Jacobian C` and to discharge each of the four protected instances
865	on it. -/
866	noncomputable def jacobianWitness (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
867	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
868	    JacobianWitness C :=
869	  Classical.choice (nonempty_jacobianWitness C)
870	
871	-- data
872	/-- The Jacobian of a smooth, proper curve over a field `k`.
873	
874	The Jacobian is the underlying scheme of an Albanese witness for `C` (see
875	`JacobianWitness` and `nonempty_jacobianWitness`), so it is `Pic⁰_{C/k}` in its étale
876	form for the witness `picardJacobianWitness`, whose remaining content is the five
877	obligations enumerated in the file header: the two étale leaves of §"The open leaves of
878	the two witnesses" together with `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` and the two residues
879	`Pic0Et.geometricallyReduced` / `Pic0Et.universallyClosed`. The genus-`0`
880	specialisation is implicit in the witness — a smooth proper geometrically
881	irreducible group scheme over `k` of relative dimension `0` is `Spec k` — so
882	no separate genus-`0` construction is needed. -/
883	noncomputable def Jacobian (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
884	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
885	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
886	  (jacobianWitness C).J
887	
888	namespace Jacobian
889	
890	/-! ## The Jacobian of `C` is an abelian variety. -/
891	
892	-- data
893	/-- The group scheme structure on the Jacobian of the curve `C`. -/
894	noncomputable instance instGrpObj : GrpObj (Jacobian C) := (jacobianWitness C).grpObj
895	
896	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is smooth of relative dimension `g` over `k`, where `g` is the
897	genus of `C`. -/
898	instance smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus : SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (Jacobian C).hom :=
899	  (jacobianWitness C).smoothGenus

763	giving smoothness of relative dimension `genus C` (`Scheme.Pic0.smooth`), properness
764	(`Scheme.Pic0.proper`), and geometric irreducibility
765	(`Scheme.Pic0.geometricallyIrreducible`); the Albanese universal property is the
766	Abel–Jacobi factorisation of `AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.AlbaneseUP`.
767	
768	The genus-`0` case is **not** special and needs no separate construction: when
769	`genus C = 0` the tangent space is `0`-dimensional, so `Pic⁰_{C/k} = Spec k`
770	automatically, and the universal property degenerates to the (then trivial) statement
771	that every pointed morphism `C ⟶ A` into an abelian variety is constant. The former

1500	* `classDegree_abel` is the characterisation: on the class of `𝒪(D)` for a relative divisor
1501	  family of constant fibre degree `d`, the value is `d`. `PicScheme.abelMap` is
1502	  `abelMapWitness` (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, sorry-free), and
1503	  `DivFamily.ClassHasFiberDeg` is the constant-fibre-degree predicate of `Picard/DivDegree.lean`.

1506	on `𝒪(D)` — the characterisation the previous docstring named — needs a divisor-to-line-bundle
1507	comparison that this project does not have at the relative level; the Abel map *is* that
1508	comparison, already built and already carrying the degree ledger
1509	(`PicScheme.abelDeg_app_mk`, `DivFamily.ClassHasFiberDeg.finrank_fiber_cokernel`). So the pin
1510	is stated where the existing structure can discharge it.
1511	
1512	THE ACCEPTANCE TEST, run before landing this — the lesson of `ClassDegree`'s own collapse and
1513	of the parallel `SymPowData` defect (inbox I-0493, 2026-07-28) is that a class must be probed
1514	with the trivial witness, so: **the zero homomorphism no longer inhabits this class**, provided

1527	is the remaining input, and it is a construction rather than a characterisation — which is a

161	automorphism lying in a commuting square over the corresponding Galois automorphism
162	`Spec γ` of the base.  (`X` is *not* acted on over `Spec L` — only the composite
163	descends to `Spec K`; this is exactly Kleiman/Milne's "descent datum" for the finite
164	Galois cover `Spec L → Spec K`.) -/
165	structure SemilinearGalAction (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) where
166	  /-- The action by scheme automorphisms. -/
167	  act : (L ≃ₐ[K] L) →* Aut X
168	  /-- Each automorphism covers the Galois action `Spec γ` on the base. -/
169	  compat (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
170	    (act γ).hom ≫ f = f ≫ (toSpecAut (L ≃ₐ[K] L) L γ).hom
171	
172	namespace SemilinearGalAction
173	
174	variable {K L}
175	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
176	
177	/-- Equivariance of a morphism between two semilinearly-acted schemes over `Spec L`. -/
178	def IsEquivariant {X' : Scheme.{u}} {f' : X' ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
179	    (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) (ρ' : SemilinearGalAction K L X' f')
180	    (h : X ⟶ X') : Prop :=
181	  ∀ γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, (ρ.act γ).hom ≫ h = h ≫ (ρ'.act γ).hom
182	
183	/-- The `Γ`-orbit of a point of `X` under a semilinear action. -/
184	def orbit (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) (x : X) : Set X :=
185	  Set.range fun γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L => (ρ.act γ).hom.base x
186	
187	/-- **Orbit-in-affine hypothesis** (campaign `G2`, audit item 8): every `Γ`-orbit is
188	contained in an affine open.  This hypothesis is **essential** (Hironaka trap — see
189	the module docstring): without it the quotient exists only as an algebraic space.
190	For finite Galois `L/K` every orbit is finite, so this is the standard EGA II 4.5.4
191	hypothesis; it holds e.g. for quasi-projective `X` (finite point sets of
192	quasi-projective schemes lie in affine opens) and is supplied to the campaign
193	consumer by the Γ-stable `V_Σ` covers of `J5`. -/
194	class OrbitsInAffineOpen (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) : Prop where
195	  exists_affineOpen (x : X) :
196	    ∃ U : X.affineOpens, ∀ γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, (ρ.act γ).hom.base x ∈ U.1
197	
198	/-- A `Γ`-stable open of `X`. -/
199	def IsStableOpen (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) (U : X.Opens) : Prop :=
200	  ∀ γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, (ρ.act γ).hom ⁻¹ᵁ U = U

1	/-
2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.
3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import Mathlib
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RelPicFunctor
8	
9	/-!
10	# The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor
11	
12	This file constructs the **étale-sheafified relative Picard functor**
13	`Pic_{(C/k)ét}` of a smooth proper curve `C/k` and proves that it *is* a sheaf
14	for the étale topology — the object whose representability is the project's
15	central open obligation (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`).
16	
17	## Why the sheafification is the right object
18	
19	The relative Picard presheaf `T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`
20	(`Scheme.PicSharp.relPresheaf`, Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`) is in general **not
21	a sheaf** (Kleiman §2, L1330: "not *a priori* a sheaf"), and over a general
22	field it is **not representable** — the witness is Exercise `ex:Pfs`, the conic
23	`u²+v²+w²=0` in `ℙ²_ℝ`, smooth proper geometrically integral with no rational
24	point.
25	
26	**CITATION CORRECTED 2026-07-29 (`review-ajc`).** This paragraph asserted
27	non-sheafness "not even for the Zariski topology (Kleiman §2, L1292–L1302)",
28	and glossed it as: a line bundle can be trivial on each member of a cover of `T`
29	without being trivial modulo `π_T^* Pic(T)`. Both the citation and the gloss are
30	wrong. L1292–L1302 proves that the **absolute** functor `Pic_X` is never a
31	separated Zariski presheaf, using `T = ℙ¹_X`; the quotient by `π_T^* Pic(T)`
32	that defines the *relative* functor is exactly what kills that argument, and
33	L1600–L1605 in fact proves `Pic_{X/S} ≅ Pic_{(X/S)zar}` when `f` has a section.
34	Sheafifying is still the right move and the conclusion below is unaffected —
35	only the stated reason was. Full account in
36	`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`'s module docstring.
37	
38	Kleiman's representability theorem (§4 Thm. `th:main`) is
39	therefore a statement about the associated **étale** sheaf, and it is that
40	statement which is true over an arbitrary base field with no rational-point
41	hypothesis.
42	
43	There are two ways to reach a sheaf, and they differ in what has to be
44	supplied:
45	
46	1. assume `C` has a `k`-rational point. Then Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 says the
47	   comparison `Pic_{C/k} → Pic_{(C/k)ét}` is already bijective, so the plain
48	   presheaf is the sheaf. This is *strictly weaker* than the challenge, whose
49	   curve need not have a rational point, and it is the route the conditional
50	   `Scheme.picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` records;
51	2. sheafify. Nothing is assumed about `C(k)`, and the sheaf axiom holds by
52	   construction. This is the route realised here and the one the project
53	   claims (owner decision of 2026-07-28).
54	
55	## The site
56	
57	Mathlib `v4.31` carries the big étale site on schemes,
58	`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleTopology = grothendieckTopology @Etale`
59	(`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean`). The relative Picard presheaf
60	lives on the slice `Over (Spec k)` rather than on `Scheme`, so the topology is
61	transported along the localisation of SGA 4 III 5.2.1, available in Mathlib as
62	`GrothendieckTopology.over`: a sieve of `T : Over (Spec k)` covers iff the
63	corresponding sieve of `T.left` covers étale-locally. That transport is where
64	"the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`" becomes a definition rather than a parameter,
65	and it is what lets the sheaf property below be a *theorem* rather than a
66	hypothesis.
67	
68	## Main definitions
69	
70	* `Scheme.etaleTopologyOver k` — the étale topology on `(Sch/k) = Over (Spec k)`.
71	* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` — `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, a bundled
72	  `Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat`, obtained by sheafifying the
73	  relative Picard presheaf.
74	* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf_isSheaf` — the sheaf property, extracted as a
75	  standalone statement about the underlying presheaf.
76	* `Scheme.PicScheme.picEt C` — the set-valued functor
77	  `T ↦ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T)` that the representability obligation is stated
78	  against, together with `picEtComparison C`, the canonical comparison
79	  `picSharp C ⟶ picEt C` from the unsheafified functor.
80	* `Scheme.PicScheme.picEt_isSheaf_forget` — the sheaf property of `picEt`
81	  itself (the group structure forgotten), which is what a representing scheme
82	  must match.
83	
84	## References
85	
86	Kleiman, "The Picard scheme" (arXiv:math/0504020), §2 Def. `df:Pfs` (the
87	étale-sheaf clause) and Thm. 2.5 (`th:comp`), §4 Thm. `th:main`.
88	Blueprint: `def:rel_pic_etale_sheafification`,
89	`thm:rel_pic_etale_sheaf_group_structure`, `sec:fga_pic_setup`.
90	-/
91	
92	set_option autoImplicit false
93	
94	universe u
95	
96	open CategoryTheory
97	
98	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
99	
100	namespace Scheme
101	
102	/-! ## §1. The étale site of `(Sch/k)` -/
103	
104	/-- **The étale topology on `(Sch/k)`.**
105	
106	The big étale topology on schemes (`Scheme.etaleTopology`, Mathlib
107	`AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean`) localised at `Spec k` along SGA 4
108	III 5.2.1 (`GrothendieckTopology.over`): a sieve of a `k`-scheme `T` is
109	covering exactly when the sieve it generates on the underlying scheme
110	`T.left` is covering for the étale topology
111	(`GrothendieckTopology.mem_over_iff`).
112	
113	This is the site on which the relative Picard presheaf of
114	`Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` lives, so it is the site whose sheafification
115	produces Kleiman's `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`. Note that the earlier
116	`PicSharp.etSheaf` of that file takes the topology as a *parameter*, for
117	want of a canonical choice; this definition supplies the canonical one, and
118	`PicSharp.etaleSheaf` below is the instantiation. -/
119	noncomputable abbrev etaleTopologyOver (k : Type u) [Field k] :
120	    GrothendieckTopology (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :=
121	  Scheme.etaleTopology.over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
122	
123	/-- The étale topology on `(Sch/k)` refines the Zariski one: a Zariski cover
124	of a `k`-scheme is an étale cover. Transported from
125	`zariskiTopology_le_etaleTopology` through the localisation, which is
126	monotone because `mem_over_iff` characterises membership by the pushed-forward
127	sieve on the underlying scheme.
128	
129	Recorded because it is the precise sense in which sheafifying étale-locally is
130	*stronger* than sheafifying Zariski-locally: a Zariski sheaf need not be an
131	étale sheaf, and the relative Picard presheaf is not even the former. -/
132	theorem zariskiTopologyOver_le_etaleTopologyOver (k : Type u) [Field k] :
133	    (Scheme.zariskiTopology.over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) ≤ etaleTopologyOver k := by
134	  intro T S hS
135	  rw [GrothendieckTopology.mem_over_iff] at hS ⊢
136	  exact Scheme.zariskiTopology_le_etaleTopology _ hS
137	
138	namespace PicSharp
139	
140	/-! ## §2. The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor -/
141	
142	/-- **The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor** `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`
143	(Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`, étale-sheaf clause).
144	
145	The associated étale sheaf of the relative Picard presheaf
146	`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` (`PicSharp.relPresheaf`), as a bundled object
147	of `Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat`. Its sheaf property is not an
148	assumption but part of the datum — `Sheaf.cond`, extracted as
149	`etaleSheaf_isSheaf` below — which is the whole point of passing to it: the
150	unsheafified `relPresheaf` is not a sheaf even Zariski-locally.
151	
152	This is a genuine instantiation of the parametric `PicSharp.etSheaf` of
153	`Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` at the canonical étale topology, with one
154	correction: `etSheaf` sheafifies the *absolute* functor `PicSharp.presheaf`
155	(`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)`), whereas Kleiman's `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` and the
156	representability theorem are about the *relative* one, `relPresheaf`. It is
157	the relative functor that is sheafified here.
158	
159	The abelian-group structure survives sheafification because the target
160	`AddCommGrpCat` has the sheafification adjunction
161	(`HasWeakSheafify` for a concrete, filtered-colimit-preserving forgetful
162	functor); `toEtaleSheaf` below is the unit. -/
163	noncomputable def etaleSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
164	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
165	    Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} :=
166	  (CategoryTheory.presheafToSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}).obj
167	    (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)
168	
169	/-- **The sheaf property of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, as a standalone statement.**
170	
171	The underlying presheaf of `PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` satisfies the sheaf axiom
172	for the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`. This is `Sheaf.cond` of the bundled
173	object, stated separately because it is the property consumers cite: a
174	representing scheme for `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` exists only because the functor being
175	represented is an étale sheaf (a representable functor is a sheaf for any
176	subcanonical topology, so a non-sheaf can never be representable — which is
177	exactly why the unsheafified `relPresheaf` needs a rational point).
178	
179	Proved, not assumed: sheafification produces a sheaf. -/
180	theorem etaleSheaf_isSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
181	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
182	    Presheaf.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (etaleSheaf C).obj :=
183	  (etaleSheaf C).property
184	
185	/-- **The comparison map** `Pic_{C/k} ⟶ Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, i.e. the unit of the
186	sheafification adjunction at the relative Picard presheaf.
187	
188	Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 (`th:comp`) says this map is an isomorphism when `C` has a
189	`k`-rational point (and `O_S = f_* O_X` universally, automatic here). Over an
190	arbitrary base field it is only a comparison: the honest object is the target,
191	which is why the representability obligation is stated there. -/
192	noncomputable def toEtaleSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
193	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
194	    PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ (etaleSheaf C).obj :=
195	  CategoryTheory.toSheafify (etaleTopologyOver k) (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)
196	
197	/-- The universal property of the sheafification, in the form consumers use:
198	every morphism from the relative Picard presheaf to (the underlying presheaf
199	of) an étale sheaf factors uniquely through `toEtaleSheaf`.
200	
201	This is what makes `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` the *canonical* choice rather than one
202	sheaf among many, and it is the step that turns a representing scheme for the
203	sheaf into a universal receiver of relative Picard classes. -/

205	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))

207	    (G : Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) :

214	namespace PicScheme
215	
216	/-! ## §3. The set-valued functor that gets represented -/
217	
218	/-- **The functor whose representability is the project's central obligation**:
219	the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor with its group structure
220	forgotten,
221	
222	```
223	picEt C : (Sch/k)^op ⥤ Type (u+1),   T ↦ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T).
224	```
225	
226	Representability is a statement about the underlying set-valued functor; the
227	group structure is transported back onto the representing scheme by Yoneda
228	(`PicScheme.groupSchemeStructure`), exactly as for the unsheafified
229	`picSharp`.
230	
231	Contrast with `picSharp C = relPresheaf C ⋙ forget`: that functor is
232	representable only under a rational-point hypothesis (it is not even a
233	Zariski sheaf otherwise), whereas *this* one is the object of Kleiman §4
234	Thm. `th:main` and its representability needs no hypothesis on `C(k)`. -/
235	noncomputable def picEt {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
236	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
237	    (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1) :=
238	  (PicSharp.etaleSheaf C).obj ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}

240	/-- The comparison `picSharp C ⟶ picEt C` of set-valued functors, the
241	set-level shadow of `PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf`. An isomorphism under a
242	`k`-rational point (Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5), a comparison in general.
243	
244	The source is written out as `PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget _` rather than as

251	    PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} ⟶ picEt C :=

253	    (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1})

cd /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge
/home/axel/.archon-env/bin/horizon inbox add --kind issue --project Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge --body "VACUITY: Pic0.Bundle (Albanese/AlbaneseUP.lean:316) is a five-field structure NONE of whose fields mention C -- the HasDivFunctor shape, one level up from the seam and NOT on the excluded list.

STATEMENT, verbatim (Albanese/AlbaneseUP.lean:316-329):
  structure Bundle {kbar : Type u} [Field kbar] [IsAlgClosed kbar]
      (C : Over (Spec (.of kbar)))
      [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
      [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] where
    scheme : Over (Spec (.of kbar))
    grpObj : GrpObj scheme
    proper : IsProper scheme.hom
    smooth : Smooth scheme.hom
    geomIrred : GeometricallyIrreducible scheme.hom

WHICH OBJECT IS ABSENT: C. Every field speaks only about the self-introduced field 'scheme'. Nothing relates 'scheme' to Pic0Scheme C, to Pic0SchemeEt C, or to C at all. So 'Bundle C' says: there EXISTS some k-bar-scheme that is a proper smooth geometrically irreducible group object. Falsifier: none -- Spec k-bar itself inhabits it (trivial group object, proper, smooth, geometrically irreducible), for EVERY C. The docstring at :313 sells it as 'Interface for Pic0_{C/k-bar}'; the type does not mention Pic0 or C.

WHY THIS IS NOT HARMLESS, and it differs from HasDivFunctor here. The type Bundle C is inhabited independent of C, but the project's actual consumer chain goes through the DEFINITION 'bundle C' (:360), which does pin scheme := Scheme.Pic0Scheme C. So jacobianScheme C := (bundle C).scheme is pinned by unfolding. The exposure is that NOTHING in the tree records that equation as a lemma: grep finds no 'jacobianScheme ... = Pic0Scheme' statement anywhere, only a docstring assertion at Jacobian.lean:668 ('Pic0.jacobianScheme C is Scheme.Pic0Scheme C, so the statements match on the nose'). The Albanese universal property at AlbaneseUP.lean:620,656,733 is stated against 'jacobianScheme C', i.e. against a projection of a structure whose type permits any group scheme. A future edit to 'bundle' (or a second producer) changes what every Albanese theorem is about with no type error and no failing lemma.

COUNTS: instances/producers = 1 (Albanese.Pic0.bundle, :360). Binder call sites of an ARBITRARY Bundle = 0 (nothing takes '(b : Bundle C)'); consumers instead take projections of the fixed 'bundle C' -- 4 direct (jacobianScheme :377, jacobianScheme_grpObj :385, jacobianScheme_isProper :389, jacobianScheme_smooth :393, jacobianScheme_geomIrred :397) and ~20 downstream references to jacobianScheme across Albanese/.

WHAT A READER IS MISLED INTO BELIEVING: that 'Bundle C' is the Pic0 interface, hence that a theorem stated about (bundle C).scheme is a theorem about the Picard identity component -- when the type alone licenses nothing about C, and the identification rests on a def-unfold plus a docstring rather than on any checked statement.

CHEAPEST REPAIR (not applied -- reviewer lane is read-only on .lean): add the pinning field or the missing lemma, e.g. 'theorem bundle_scheme : (bundle C).scheme = Scheme.Pic0Scheme C := rfl'. One line, and it converts the docstring claim at Jacobian.lean:668 into a checked fact. This is the same repair ClassDegreePinned made after ClassDegree's collapse (Picard/IdentityComponent.lean:1532).

Reported by review-ajc, vacuity/self-projection scan, 2026-07-30. Statements read at HEAD."
